actor_execution:
Actor execution loop system (248565–250157, Bank 03).

Contains the complete actor update pipeline — five distinct execution contexts that the main game loop calls to process active actors each frame, plus actor/thinker pool initialization and scene actor spawning infrastructure.

=== EXECUTION CONTEXTS ===

Five actor processing modes selected by game state flags:

1. RunActors_Normal (248565): Standard gameplay. Strips the attack button ($0080) from joypadCurrent while playerFlags bit 3 (combat lock, $0008) is set, then checks playerFlags for terrain shake ($0010) → PauseFiltered, or displayModeFlags ($0080) → DisplayFiltered. Processes each actor in the linked list ($56 head → $06 next). For each actor: sets DP/X to slot, runs either the script-driven path ($10 bit 13 set) or the iframe-managed path (bit 13 clear), dispatches to the actor's script via the RTL trick ($00:$02), then applies post-tick movement. Callers: main loop (system_core), scene_lifecycle (two settle ticks) and inventory_overlay (two layout ticks).

2. RunActors_DisplayFiltered (248739): Active when displayModeFlags bit 7 set. Only processes actors with bit 12 ($1000) set in primary ($10) or secondary ($12) flags.

3. RunActors_PauseFiltered (248893): Active when playerFlags bit 4 ($0010, terrain shake) set. Only processes actors with $12 bits 12|2 ($1004) or $10 bits 12|10 ($1400). Has a special iframe-only tail for non-immune actors.

4. RunActors_CutsceneOnly (249087): Cutscene playback. Only processes actors with $10 bit 11 ($0800). Clears bit 2 each frame. Called only from system_core's re-entrant frame helper (used by COP handlers that must keep the screen alive).

5. RunActors_OverlayOnly (249198): Overlay rendering. Checks display filter first. Only processes actors with $12 bit 12 ($1000). Always uses simple ApplyMovement (no collision). Called only from system_core's UpdateFrameFull, which the NMI runs while the blocking SPC music upload is in progress (so overlay actors keep animating during the upload).

=== COP SCRIPT DISPATCH ===

All contexts use the same indirect call mechanism: PHK / PEA PostTick-1 / SEP #$20 / LDA $02 (bank) / PHA / REP #$20 / LDA $00 (addr-1) / PHA / RTL. This pushes a return address and a target address; RTL pops the target and jumps. The -1 adjustments account for RTL adding 1.

=== IFRAME COUNTER ($7F0028,X) ===

Signed hit counter, handled only when bit 7 ($0080) of $10 is set and (in RunActors_Normal/DisplayFiltered/PauseFiltered) bit 13 ($2000) is clear. Positive = hit-stun (set by ApplyPlayerHitstun to $3C and by combat_collision to $0011): each tick DECs it and every actor except the player skips the rest of its tick (no script, no wait-counter, no movement), so hit victims freeze; the player is exempt here (its own movement code applies the freeze). Negative = recovery/invincibility (written as $FFC4, $FFE2, $FFEF, $FFF4 by the hit code): each tick INCs it toward zero while the actor keeps running, and combat_collision skips victims whose counter is negative. When the counter is zero the tick clears $0080. docs/wram-memory-map.md describes the same sign convention ("positive = stunned, absolute value = frames remaining").

=== ACTOR/THINKER POOL (InitActorPool, 249308) ===

Initializes both pools. Actor pool: 84 slots of $30 bytes at $1000–$1FBF (the slot address is the actor's direct page); free list at $0E00 addressed by the long pointer $4E/$50 ($50 = bank 0, not a count). Per-slot extended data is indexed by the slot address: $7F:0000+slot (= $7F1000–$7F1FBF; scratch, spriteset, stats, enemyNum, HP, iframes) and $7F:1000+slot (= $7F2000–$7F2FBF; onHit/onDeath/onCollide callbacks and scratch). Thinker pool: 16 slots of $10 bytes at $0F00–$0FFF; free list at $7E:3000 (long pointer $52/$54). Scene $FF (the inventory screen, see inventory_overlay) uses a simplified clear that skips $7F2000 and $7F3000.

ThinkerPoolAlloc reads the next free thinker slot via indirect long [$52], returns it in Y with carry clear, or returns carry set if the pool is exhausted. Called by SpawnSceneThinkers (thinker_execution) and COP handlers (SpawnThinker/SpawnThinkerParam).

=== SCENE SPAWNING (SpawnSceneActors, 249505) ===

Reads the scene_actors table (indexed by sceneTableIndex = scene × 2) to spawn actors. Each actor: allocate slot via ActorPoolAllocator, link into doubly-linked list ($04/$06), call InitActorFromSceneData to parse the binary record.

=== DEFEATED ENEMY HANDLING (AdvanceSceneDataAndFree, 249588) ===

Called when CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag determines an actor was already killed (flag set in wramFlags). Advances the scene data pointer past the 9-byte record, then either re-uses the same slot for the next record (if more actors follow: branches back into InitActorFromSceneData) or, when the list ends, returns the allocated slot to the free list, unlinks it from the actor chain, and decrements activeActorCount.

=== ACTOR RECORD FORMAT (InitActorFromSceneData, 249627) ===

Variable-length record: 7 bytes without stats, 9 bytes when byte 6 is nonzero. Byte 0-1 = X/Y tile (×16→pixels), byte 2 = type flags (bit 0 = addressing mode), bytes 3-4 = code pointer, byte 5 = bank, byte 6 = stats index (0 = no stats, record ends here), byte 7 = enemy number, byte 8 = event-block index (stored as deathActionIdx; the name is historical — see CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag and StageBgChangeFromDeathIdx). Player actors (bit 15 of $10) get special init: load character form body table, set spriteset, compute camera centering.

Enemies with nonzero enemyNum are checked against the enemy-defeat flags in wramFlags (CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag). The flags are cleared only when the world map is entered, at a few scripted points and on game over, not at every scene change (see flag_helpers, OQ-67). Already-defeated actors are freed via AdvanceSceneDataAndFree and their event block tiles are swapped.
combat_collision:
Combat and interaction collision system (244613–247295, Bank 03).

Implements all actor-vs-actor collision detection and damage processing. Called from the main game loop after actor AI execution and sprite composition. Contains two independent collision pipelines (combat and interaction), plus shared helpers for knockback, damage formatting, and death handling.

=== COLLISION PIPELINE OVERVIEW ===

The system uses the actor render list ($0C00, word-sized entries) as its iteration source — only actors in the render list are candidates for collision. This means off-screen actors are never tested.

1. RunCombatCollision (244708): Outer entry point. Checks player's orb flag ($0040 in $10) — if set, no combat occurs. Otherwise iterates the render list in CombatCollision_EnemyLoop.

2. RunInteractionCollision (246366): Separate entry for NPC/object interactions. Tests player bounding box (±4px X, −4/−14px Y from position) against interaction hitboxes. Checks $2040 (COP mode + orb) to skip, and $0280 to route to FriendlyMode.

=== COMBAT COLLISION (244729–245081) ===

Two-phase collision detection:

Phase 1 (outer loop): For each enemy in the render list, for each actor WITHOUT $0400, requires $0080 set in $10 (role unresolved, OQ-8), $0040 clear (not dead/orb) and $12 $0010 clear (not damage-immune). If eligible, calls PlayerAttackHitTest.

Phase 2 (inner loop at CombatCollision_InnerLoop): After player attack processing, checks all actors against the current enemy's hitbox for enemy-hits-player collision. Uses AABB overlap testing on hitbox fields ($20–$23). Two paths based on $20 flag: normal ($76E0 exclusion mask) or friendly ($74E0 mask + extendedFlags $0010 check).

=== HITBOX FORMAT ===

Hitboxes are stored in the metasprite header at $0004–$0007 as signed 8-bit offsets:
- $0004: X offset from actor position (sign-extended via $0080 check)
- $0005: X width (added to offset for right edge)
- $0006: Y offset (sign-extended)
- $0007: Y height (added to offset for bottom edge)

The ASL ASL on $000E,X extracts the H-mirror flag from the actor's sprite field, which flips the hitbox X coordinates (BCS path negates offsets).

=== DAMAGE FORMULAS ===

Player attacks enemy (PlayerAttackHitTest):
  damage = chainDamage/2 + 1
  enemyHP = max(0, enemyHP − damage)
  chainDamage stored at $7F101E,X accumulates across consecutive hits

Phase-2 hit (ApplyHitDamageToVictim: uses the PLAYER's strength and reduces the overlapped actor's HP):
  totalStr = playerStr + bonus + climbStateData      (bonus = $09E2, 0 when the hitter is actor slot $1000)
  rawDamage = max(1, totalStr − victimStats[2])      (stats table: [0] max HP, [1] ATK, [2] DEF)
  damage = rawDamage + characterForm
  victimHP = max(0, victimHP − damage)

Actor touches player (ApplyInteractionDamage):
  damage = max(1, attackerStats[1] − playerDef); playerHp = max(0, playerHp − damage)

=== DEATH HANDLING ===

Normal victims get HitStaggerMain spawned and are resolved later in hit_stagger_controller's HitStaggerResolveHit (HP == 0: set $0040, run onDeathCallback ($7F1004,X) or StandardEnemyDefeatHandler). Only victims that skip the stagger (stagger-immune $12 $0010, or playerFlags $0010 terrain shake) are resolved inline here: HP == 0 sets $0040 and either uses onDeathCallback or dispatches StandardEnemyDefeatHandler and sets $0400 (standard defeat flag).

=== IFRAME ASSIGNMENT ===

After damage: checks $12 bit 0 ($0001). If set, assigns iframeCounter = $FFEF (negative = recovery: counts up toward zero, the tick still runs). If clear, assigns $0011 (positive = hit-stun: non-player actors skip their tick, the player's tick still runs). The counter is handled by RunActors_Normal for actors without $10 bit 13 ($2000); a script-driven actor (bit 13 set) takes the script path and ignores it. Plays hit sound #05.

=== KNOCKBACK ===

CalcKnockbackDirection (246082): Computes the midpoint of the attacker's hitbox, compares against the target's center position, and returns a cardinal direction (0=S, 1=N, 2=W, 3=E) based on which axis has the greater delta. Falls back to GetPlayerFacing if the attacker is the player.

CalcKnockbackFromActorCenters (247076): Similar but uses raw actor centers (position ± 4px) instead of hitbox midpoints. Used by ApplyInteractionDamage.

=== INTERACTION COLLISION (246366–246996) ===

Two modes:
- Normal mode: Tests actors without $35C0 flags against player bbox. On hit, checks extendedFlags $0010 (collision callback). If callback exists, overwrites actor entry point. Otherwise defaults to smooth_follow_child.SmoothFollowChildDie.
- Friendly mode ($0280): Only tests actors with $0020 flag (friendly/NPC). Simplified hitbox test (no H-mirror).

ApplyInteractionDamage (246752): For combat actors ($0020 clear), calculates damage = max(1, enemyAtk − playerDef), subtracts from playerHp, spawns HitStaggerMain with knockback. For NPCs ($0020 set), routes to InteractionDamage_NPCChat.

=== NPC CHAT (246997) ===

InteractionDamage_NPCChat: Attempts GiveItemToPlayer with chatPtr. On inventory full, shows overflow message. Otherwise shows dialogue and converts the actor to NpcDespawnStub (sets $0700 in flags to prevent re-interaction).

=== DAMAGE DISPLAY ===

FormatDamageDigits (247183): Converts a 16-bit damage number to packed BCD format for sprite-based display. Handles values up to 999 (returns carry set for ≥1000). Digits packed as: high byte = hundreds, bits 7-4 of low byte = tens, bits 3-0 = ones. SpawnDamageNumberEffect actors display the formatted digits as floating damage numbers.
ConsoleStringRenderer:
Console string renderer — bytecode-driven HUD/UI text and widget system (256610–257943, Bank 03).

Implements a complete rendering engine for non-dialogue text output: inventory screens, status displays, HP bars, equipment icons, and bordered UI boxes. Separate from the wide-string dialogue renderer (DialogStringRenderer at 254549) — this system uses a simpler 8-bit character set where bytes >= $12 are literal tile indices written directly to the VRAM staging buffer, and bytes $00–$11 are command opcodes dispatched through an 18-entry command table.

=== RENDERING ARCHITECTURE ===

Entry point: ConsoleStringRenderer, called via JSL. Y = string data pointer (in the current data bank), X = VRAM buffer write position (byte offset into $7F0200, one tilemap row = $40 bytes). Each character writes a 16-bit VRAM tilemap word: low byte = tile index, high byte = attribute (palette/priority/flip) from sceneStateHelper ($099F).

Display state: $099E/$099F form one 16-bit attribute word (the low byte is always 0 in the vanilla game, the high byte is sceneStateHelper). The multi-tile commands (numbers, boxes, fills, raw bytes) OR $099E into each tile word. $09A0 is the line-start cursor: SetVramAddr and DrawBox set it, and the two row-advance commands move it by a whole row and make it the new cursor, so a line break returns to the column of the last position command, not the current column.

The command dispatch uses JSR ($addr,X) — indirect indexed JSR through ConsoleStringCommandTable. Commands may recursively call ConsoleStringRenderer (InsertRemoteString, IndirectString, InsertSharedWord) and return the new X by writing it to the saved-X slot on the stack ($03,S, or $05,S after one extra PHY).

Operand addresses (digit sources, counts, index variables) are 16-bit offsets in the CURRENT data bank, so they only reach RAM because banks $00–$3F mirror WRAM $0000–$1FFF. Callers set the data bank to the string's bank.

=== COMMAND TABLE ($00–$11) ===

The "Tag" column is the name used in the ConsoleString text syntax (db-us/stringTypes.json). In the vanilla strings (tables/system_strings) the commands STR, CLR, CPY and UNK never occur, and BCD occurs once with one digit; the retranslation/patch strings may use more.

| Cmd | Tag | Handler | Operand | Description |
|-----|-----|---------|---------|-------------|
| $00 | (end) | End | — | Pop registers, RTL to caller |
| $01 | POS | SetVramAddr | 2B word | Set the cursor (and line start) to a buffer offset; the text form writes it as low byte, high byte |
| $02 | STR | InsertRemoteString | 2B addr + 1B bank | Recursive render from another bank |
| $03 | PAL | SetPalette | 1B bits | Set palette bits 2-4 in the attribute byte |
| $04 | TBL | IndirectString | 2B table + 1B bank + 2B index address | Render the string selected by a RAM index |
| $05 | BCD | PrintBcdNumber | 1B digit count + 2B addr | Packed BCD digits, low digit first in memory, printed right-to-left |
| $06 | BOX | DrawBox | 1B w + 1B h + 2B pos | Bordered rectangle with corners/edges/fill |
| $07 | CLR | ClearColumn | 2B pos | Blank a block whose width is measured from the existing tiles |
| $08 | CPY | FillTile | 1B tile + 2B count address | Write a tile N times (N read from RAM) |
| $09 | UNK | PrintEquipIcons | var (term $80+) | 2×2 equipment metatiles (no use found in the extracted strings) |
| $0A | HP | DrawPlayerHpBar | — | Player HP as full/half/empty segments |
| $0B | HE | DrawEnemyHpBar | — | Enemy HP bar (same algorithm, different palette) |
| $0C | ESC | PrintRawBytes | var (term $FF) | Raw tile bytes until terminator |
| $0D | DBL | DoubleNewLine | — | Line break of 2 tilemap rows: cursor = line start + $0080 |
| $0E | NUM | Print3DigitNumber | 2B addr | 16-bit value at addr as up to 3 decimal digits |
| $0F | RCC | ClearRect | 1B width + 1B height | Blank (width+1) × (height+1) tiles; must be the last command before the end byte |
| $10 | LU | InsertSharedWord | 1B index | Insert entry N of shared_word_table (shared words such as 'Crystal ', 'Psycho '; used by item and ability names alike) |
| $11 | N | NewLine | — | Line break of 1 tilemap row: cursor = line start + $0040 |

=== HP BAR SYSTEM ===

DrawPlayerHpBar/DrawEnemyHpBar share DrawHpBar for rendering. HP is divided into three segment types:
- Full segments ($00): playerHp/2, tile $2006 (filled)
- Half segment ($08): 1 if HP is odd, tile $2007 (half-filled)
- Empty segments ($02): (maxHP − HP)/2, tile $20FF (empty)

The bar is at most 40 half-units (20 segments). The clamp is written back to the source variable, and the current HP is only clamped when the maximum had to be clamped. Bars wrap to a second row via HpBar_AdvanceRow after 10 tiles. Player uses palette $0800 (palette 2), enemy uses $0400 (palette 1).

=== DRAW BOX ===

Constructs a bordered rectangle (width × height interior, so width+2 by height+2 tiles) using 4 tile types: $10 (corners, with V/H flip bits for each corner), $11 (horizontal edges), $12 (vertical edges), $40 (interior fill). All OR'd with the $099E attribute word. After drawing, the cursor is set to box start + $0082 (2 rows down, 1 column right).

=== EQUIPMENT ICONS ===

PrintEquipIcons renders variable-length equipment lists as 2×2 metatiles, 2 tiles wide each. Items 0-7 use tile base $01E0, items 8+ use $02E0 (2 tiles per icon in the tile sheet). Each icon writes 4 tiles: upper-left (N), upper-right (N+1), lower-left (N+$10), lower-right (N+$11); the upper pair goes in the row above the cursor, the lower pair in the cursor row.
DialogStringRenderer:
Wide-string dialogue renderer and dialogue box management (254549–256073, Bank 03).

Implements the complete text rendering pipeline for IOG's dialogue system. The engine processes a bytecode-driven wide-string format where characters below $C0 are tile indices rendered directly to a VRAM staging buffer, and bytes $C0–$FF are command opcodes dispatched through a 25-entry command table.

=== DIALOG STRING RENDERER (254549) ===

Entry point: DialogStringRenderer, called via JSL from COP script handlers and other engine systems.

The renderer maintains state in work RAM:
- $0998: Current VRAM buffer write cursor (X index into $7F0200)
- $0986: Palette bits (OR'd into each tile word, shifted left by XBA + ASL ×2)
- $097A/$097C: Dialogue box column/row position
- $097E/$0980: Saved column/row origin for cursor calculations
- $099A: VRAM buffer base offset (start of current dialogue box content area)
- $099C: Current line number within the dialogue box
- $0996: Per-character sound effect ID
- $007E: Frame delay between characters (controls text speed)
- $0B04: Saved frame delay value (restored on box open/close)
- $00EE: Menu-mode flag (written by the diary menu); when nonzero the box omits its extra prompt/scroll row
- $00DC: Cleared on every box open; no reader found (purpose unproven)

Strings are read through DBR (absolute LDA $0000,Y), so DBR must be the string's bank. The recursive commands (InsertTemplate, InsertRemoteString, DictionaryA/B) switch DBR themselves.

Each character tile is written to two VRAM buffer rows: $7F0200,X (top half) and $7F0240,X (bottom half). The bottom-half tile index is the top index + $10, the next row of 16 tiles in the font sheet (inferred). This produces 16×16 pixel characters from pairs of 8×8 tiles.

The command dispatch uses an RTS trick: PEA pushes the loop return address (DialogString_CharLoop − 1), then the command table address − 1 is pushed and RTS jumps to it. Commands return via RTS back to the character loop.

=== COMMAND TABLE (254659) ===

25 commands indexed 0x00–0x18:
- $C0 EndAndWait: Wait for input, clear box, restore frame delay
- $C1 SetPosition: Set column/row from 2-byte operand
- $C2 InsertTemplate: Recursively render a template string from dialog_template_table
- $C3 SetPalette: Set palette bits from 1-byte operand
- $C4 InfiniteLoop: Halt (NOP NOP BRA self)
- $C5 IndirectString: Read string pointer from an indirect table (4-byte operand)
- $C6 PrintNumber: Print a packed-BCD number as digit tiles (4-byte operand: digit-count word, then the address of the number data)
- $C7 OpenDialogueBox: Open a custom-sized dialogue box (2-byte operand: width, height)
- $C8 ClearDialogueBox: Clear box contents, reset palette to default, wait one frame
- $C9 WaitFrames: Pause for N frames (1-byte operand)
- $CA Return: Exit the renderer (pop call stack, PLP, RTL)
- $CB NewLine: Advance to next line; scroll up if at bottom
- $CC AdvanceCursor: Move cursor forward by N tiles (1-byte operand)
- $CD InsertRemoteString: Render a string from another bank (3-byte operand: address + bank)
- $CE ClearBox: Clear box interior (keep border), reset cursor
- $CF WaitForButton: Wait for a button in mask $C040 (logical $8000/$4000/$0040) with a blinking cursor, then clear the box
- $D0 WaitForAnyInput: Wait for a button in mask $C040
- $D1 JumpToAddress: Set Y to new string address (2-byte operand)
- $D2 SetSfx: Set per-character sound effect (1-byte operand)
- $D3 OpenDefaultBox: Open standard 13×4 dialogue box at position (3, 17)
- $D4 SetPaletteColor: Write a 15-bit color to CGRAM (3-byte operand: index + color)
- $D5 SetFrameDelay: Set text speed (1-byte operand, +2 bias)
- $D6 DictionaryA: Insert a word from dialog_dictionary_a (1-byte operand)
- $D7 DictionaryB: Insert a word from dialog_dictionary_b (1-byte operand)
- $D8 PrintRawTiles: Output raw tile bytes until zero terminator

=== DIALOGUE BOX RENDERING ===

DialogCmd_OpenDialogueBox (255039) and DialogCmd_OpenDefaultBox (255735) construct the box frame:
1. Set border tile pointer to DialogueBorderTiles (8 tiles: corners + edges)
2. DrawDialogueBorderRow renders top/bottom borders
3. DrawDialogueBodyRows fills interior rows with blank tiles ($2040) and side borders
4. An extra blank row (room for the continuation cursor and for scrolling) is appended when worldReadyFlag is set and the menu-mode flag $00EE is zero

The VRAM staging buffer at $7F0200 mirrors the 32-tile-wide BG3 tilemap: one tile row is $40 bytes (32 words), so $7F0240 is the next tilemap row. A character is two rows tall, hence a text line is $80 bytes. Box position is computed as: base = (row × 32 + column) × 2 bytes; XBA + LSR + LSR turns row into row × $40.

GetPlayerFacingDirection:
Player facing direction lookup — animation-frame-to-direction mapping with form support (258250–258512, Bank 03).

Determines the player's current facing direction (0–3 = down/up/left/right, the operand order of the facing COP ops) from the player actor's animation frame index ($0028,X), so scripts and enemy AI can ask which way the player is looking. Forms that replace the body sprite use their own per-form frame tables.

=== ALGORITHM ===

1. Load playerActor and test playerFlags bit 15 ($8000). That bit is the sprite-override flag (set by SetPlayerSpriteDirect, the transformations and ability poses), not a "transformed" flag as such.
2. Bit clear: look up FacingDirectionLookup[$0028,X]. Values 0–3 are cardinal directions; 4 means no facing for that frame.
3. Bit set: take $0AC8 (the body_table index last written by SetPlayerSpriteDirect), subtract 4, and index FacingFormOffsetTable with it; the selected table is read at the same animation frame. If $0AC8 < 4 the subtraction is negative and the code falls back to FacingDirectionLookup (step 2).
4. Return: carry clear = valid direction (0–3 in A), carry set = no facing (value ≥ 4).

=== DATA TABLES ===

FacingDirectionLookup (88 bytes): maps each animation frame of the normal body sprite to a direction 0–4.

FacingFormOffsetTable: 4 pointers, indexed by body_table index − 4, i.e. spriteset_will_abilities, spriteset_transform_poses, spriteset_freedan_fx, spriteset_shadow_fx (body_table 4–7). The FacingData_* labels follow the same order (WillAbilities, TransformPoses, FreedanFx, ShadowFx).

FacingData_WillAbilities (27 bytes) is the first table (body 4), FacingData_TransformPoses (44 bytes, all zero) the second (body 5), FacingData_FreedanFx (4 bytes, all zero) the third (body 6), FacingData_ShadowFx (6 bytes, all zero) the fourth (body 7). All entries of the last three are 0, i.e. those poses always report direction 0 (down in the COP operand order).
GlobalInputHandler:
Main UI input dispatcher — menu, map, and item use button handling (229376–229567, Bank 03).

Called once per frame from the main game loop (system_core) between warp/chest checks and actor execution. Handles the three primary UI buttons: Start (map/radar), Select (inventory), and the item-use button (Y $4000 in the vanilla game; this baserom's button-remap patch tests logical bit $0008 instead, applied through transforms.json).

=== GUARD CONDITIONS ===

Five checks suppress all input before button dispatch:
1. sceneNext nonzero — a scene transition is pending; ignore all UI input
2. playerFlags bit 9 ($0200) — game over sequence active
3. IsMusicPlaying returns carry set — a melody item is playing (SPC transfer in progress)
4. playerFlags bits 13|11 ($2800) — guard/channel stance ($2000) or script/ability lock ($0800); blocks Select and Y but NOT Start
5. No recognized button pressed — returns immediately

Note: the Start button ($1000) check comes before the $2800 guard, so the map is accessible even while blocking or during an ability.

=== BUTTON DISPATCH ===

- Start ($1000) → Map/Radar screen (toggle: stays up until Start is pressed again)
- Select ($2000) → Inventory screen (OpenInventoryScreen)
- Item use (vanilla Y $4000, logical $0008 here) → Use equipped item (ItemUseDispatch)

=== MAP/RADAR SCREEN ===

Two display modes based on playerFlags bit 3 ($0008, combat lock — set in non-combat scenes):

1. Normal mode (bit 3 clear): Calls RadarScreenSetup for the full radar minimap with actor dots, scene markers, and enemy clear reward display.

2. Combat-lock mode (bit 3 set): Displays a 'PAUSE' text overlay via BG3 script (consolestring_01EAC6) with dimmed brightness (INIDISP = $09). Used in non-combat scenes (towns, cutscene rooms) where the full radar overlay is not appropriate.

Both modes enter a shared display loop: each frame enables NMI, waits for VBlank, animates the radar border tiles, and polls joypadCurrent for a fresh Start press. Start was marked consumed in joypadHeld on entry, so joypadCurrent hides it until the button is released and pressed again; the overlay therefore stays up until that second press (a toggle, not hold-to-view). Then the overlay is torn down: VRAM buffer is partially cleared, brightness restored to $0F, displayModeFlags bit 0 set to flush pending VRAM, and one UpdateFrameDialogue call restores the normal display.

=== INVENTORY SCREEN ===

Marks Select as consumed in joypadHeld ($2000 via TSB), syncs to VBlank, calls OpenInventoryScreen, then marks both Select ($2000) and vanilla Y ($4000) as consumed on return ($6000) to prevent an immediate re-trigger of the inventory or item use. This constant is not covered by the baserom's button-remap transforms, so the logical item-use bit $0008 is not consumed here.
hdma_dma_spc:
DMA, HDMA, and SPC audio utility routines (252033–252182 + 254128–254549 + 258512–258561, Bank 03).

A mixed utility block spanning three non-contiguous address ranges, providing hardware transfer and audio infrastructure used by the scene lifecycle, NMI handler, and actor/thinker systems.

=== PLAYER TILE DMA (252033–252182) ===

DmaPlayerTilesToVram uploads the player's queued 16×16 sprite tiles from WRAM to VRAM. ClearSceneState calls it during scene loading and the NMI handler calls it whenever displayModeFlags bit 3 is set (in that NMI it replaces DmaAdhocVramBlock and the write-queue flush). The list at $06FE is one bank byte (playerTileDmaBank) followed by word pointers; each pointer addresses 64 bytes of upper-half tile rows and the lower half lies $0200 bytes further on. Four passes: upper halves of the first 8 pointers to VRAM $4000, upper halves of the pointers after the 8th (until a zero pointer) to $4200, lower halves to $4100, lower-half continuation to $4300.

=== PALETTE-BUNDLE ANIMATION (254128–254278) ===

LoadPaletteBundle and CopyPaletteBundleFrame are the two halves of one palette-animation step. Only the five palette-bundle COP handlers (#36–#3A, cop_handlers_palette) call them. A bundle (palette_bundles table, ROM bank $96) is a list of 6-byte sub-entries, and each sub-entry is an animation STRIP of N frames: byte 0 = frame count N (0 ends the bundle), bytes 1–2 = address in bank $96 of the first frame's colors, byte 3 = first CGRAM color index (destination = $7F0A00 + 2 × index, the palette staging buffer), byte 4 = frame size − 1 in bytes ($0D = 7 colors, $03 = 2 colors, $02 = one 3-byte backdrop RGB triplet), byte 5 = extra ticks to wait between frames. The frames of a strip are stored back to back (a strip with N = 8 and byte 4 = 3 is followed by exactly 32 bytes of colors, then the next sub-entry's data), and every step overwrites the same destination with the next frame. LoadPaletteBundle fills the actor fields from the next sub-entry (N → spritesetPtr, source → chatPtr, destination → metaspritePtr, size − 1 → $7F0008, wait → DP $08 and animScratch); CopyPaletteBundleFrame (nothing is decompressed and VRAM is not touched) block-moves one frame with the RAM stub at $0402 (PHB / MVN $7F,$96 / PLB / RTS, written by system_init) and advances chatPtr to the next frame. The 14 shipped sub-entries with byte 4 = 2 write the backdrop triplet: LoadPaletteBundle then adds $0200 to the destination so $7F0A00 + $0200 = backdropColors ($7F0C00).

=== HDMA CHANNEL MANAGEMENT (254278–254378) ===

ResetHdmaState (called by every frame routine: the main loop, UpdateFrameDialogue, UpdateFrameRender, UpdateFrameFull and the scene-start sequence, always after the type-A/C thinkers and before the type-B/D ones) clears the allocation state: enable mask $66 = 0, next channel bit $68 = $02 (channel 1), register block offset $6A = $10. $6C is a one-shot lock: when negative the reset is skipped once; scene_lifecycle's wave transition calls ResetHdmaState explicitly, arms $6C = $FF and runs ApplyScrollWaveEffect, whose UpdateFrameDialogue call then skips its reset (and clears $6C) so the HDMA the wave just bound survives that frame.

SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect and SetupHdmaChannel_Direct bind the next free channel (1–7): A = bank byte (low) | B-bus register number (high), Y = table address. The register number indexes hdma_channel_config to get the DMAP transfer mode (the indirect entry ORs $40 and also writes the table bank to DASB). Both finish in a shared tail that writes BBADx, A1Tx and A1Bx, sets the channel's bit in the enable mask and advances $68/$6A. The tail's ADC #$10 has no CLC: the carry is the carry-out of ASL $0068, which is clear for channels 1–6, so seven channels is the maximum (binding the 7th leaves $6A = $81).

=== SPC MUSIC CHANGE (254378–254549) ===

StartMusic and FadeThenStartMusic (cop_handlers_audio) spawn a thinker that enters at SpcTransferMusicData or SpcFadeOutHandshake with the music ID in chatPtr. The thinker talks to the SPC sound engine through port commands on APUIO0 (docs/audio/spc-disassembly.md, ProcessPortCommand): $F1 = CmdFadeOut (sets the engine's fade counters $30/$31 to $FF), $F0 = CmdStop, $FF = jump into the engine's resident clone of the IPL loader (sub_0f89), which posts $BBAA and speaks the boot-ROM upload protocol; $01 enters the engine's ASL-to-$02 path (ClearAramTail, stream pointer from ARAM $0FFC). OQ-61 is answered here: SpcFadeOutHandshake's $F1 IS the fade-out request, performed inside the SPC engine, not by 65816 code (whether the fade is audible before the following $01/$F0 commands is OQ-I021-2).

Sequence: the thinker stages the ID in musicTransitionState; the main loop's LoadMusicFromTransitionState (once per pass, after UpdateHUD) turns it into a music_pointer_array entry, enables NMI and joypad and runs spc_transfer.SpcBlockTransfer (blocking; the NMI calls UpdateFrameFull each frame meanwhile), then stores $FFFF, which releases the thinker: it waits two actor ticks (COP WaitByte #01 = N + 1 ticks: a plain delay, not an SPC acknowledgment), sends $01, clears sfxQueueCh1 and musicTransitionState and dies.

=== AD-HOC VRAM DMA (258512–258561) ===

DmaAdhocVramBlock executes one-shot VRAM transfers queued at $7F0C03–$7F0C09 (source word, source bank, destination word = trigger, byte count). It only runs from the NMI handler, which has just programmed VMAIN = $80, DMAP0 = $01 and BBAD0 = $18 for it, and it is skipped when dmaSkipFlag is set or when displayModeFlags bit 3 selected the player-tile path instead. Writers must store the size before the destination (the destination arms the transfer; OQ-64).
inventory_mgmt:
Inventory management (Bank 03, 257943-258249): give an item or pickup (GiveItemToPlayer), remove an item by id (RemoveItemFromInventory) and test whether an item is held (CheckInventoryForItem).

=== CALLERS ===

GiveItemToPlayer has 10 JSL sites in 5 files: the COP GiveItem handler (cop_handlers_inventory), chests (warps_interaction), the NPC / pickup touch handler (combat_collision.InteractionDamage_NPCChat, which gives the gem and heal drops of EnemyDropSystem), item_use_system and pyCD_puzzle (6). RemoveItemFromInventory and CheckInventoryForItem are reached only through their COP handlers.

=== ITEM ID ENCODING (A, low byte) ===

$00 to $7F: regular items, stored in the first free slot of the 16-byte inventorySlots ($0AB4). $80 = HP Max Up, $81 = STR Up, $82 = DEF Up (each +1). $83 / $84 / $85 = 1 / 2 / 5 gems (gemCount capped at 999). $86 and above = heal: hpToHeal += 5 plus the SpawnItemSparkleEffect effect. After the PHP / SEP #$20 prologue the code tests bit 7 of the id and, for specials, subtracts $80 and walks a DEC chain.

=== STAT-UP ITEMS ===

Each one clears displayModeFlags bit $0080 (leave the display-filter actor mode, in which RunActors_Normal runs only actors flagged $1000; the chest code in warps_interaction sets it around the call), plays SFX $25, adds 1 to the 8-bit stat and returns with Y = 0. The add is 8-bit signed: only when the old value is $7F does the overflow flag trigger and the stat is set to $55 (85) instead. That is a reset, not a cap: below $7F and above it (wrapping at $FF to 0) the stat is unbounded. The old note called it a cap at $55.
HP Max Up also sets hpToHeal := new max HP - HP (an 8-bit difference), so UpdateHUD refills the bar to the new maximum at 1 HP every 8 frames. STR Up and DEF Up do not touch hpToHeal.

=== OTHER SPECIAL ITEMS ===

Gems add 1, 2 or 5 to gemCount, clamp at $03E7 and play SFX $22. The heal ($86 and above) adds 5 to hpToHeal, switches D to the calling actor (D := X) so that COP SpawnListAppend( SpawnItemSparkleEffect, #00, #00, flags $2F00 ) creates the sparkle at that actor, and plays SFX $22. X must therefore be the calling actor's slot on this path. Neither the gems nor the heal change Y or $0DB8.

=== RETURN CONVENTION ===

Carry clear = given, carry set = inventory full. Regular items: Y = dialog_item_found (success), $0DB8 = item id ($0DB9 = 0) for the dialogue text; full inventory: Y = dialog_item_full, $0DB8 = item id. Stat-ups return Y = 0; gems and the heal leave Y as the caller had it, so a caller must not show Y for ids of $80 and above. P is restored (PLP).
RemoveItemFromInventory: first slot equal to A is zeroed and, only then, inventoryEquippedType := 0 and inventoryEquippedIndex := $FFFF (nothing equipped); a missing id changes nothing, and in both cases carry is restored by the PLP (the routine reports nothing). CheckInventoryForItem: carry clear = found, carry set = not found.

item_use_system:
Item use dispatch and handler system (230416–237738, Bank 03).

Contains the complete inventory item usage pipeline. When the player activates an equipped item, ItemUseDispatch reads the slot index, extracts the 6-bit item ID ($00–$3F), and dispatches through a 64-entry jump table to the appropriate handler. Each handler returns via RTS into ItemUseEpilogue, which runs a dialogue frame update and consumes the use-item button again so the press cannot re-trigger the item.

=== HANDLER PATTERNS ===

1. Display-only: Print a description and return. No gameplay effect. Used for story items (Lance Letter, Lilly Necklace, Will, Crystal Ring, Prize Money, Black Glasses, Bill & Lola Letter, Father's Journal).

2. Scene-gated key items: Check sceneCurrent for the target location, verify the player's tile position via BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles, then activate (remove item, set event flag, optionally modify tilemap). Prints failure message if location doesn't match. Used for keys (Prison, Elevator, Mine A/B, Seaside Palace), placement items (Diamond Block, Inca Statues A/B, Crystal Ball, Purification Stone, Statue of Hope, Rama Statue, Magic Powder, Teapot), and consumable quest items (Smoked Meat, Mushroom Water, Gorgon Flower).

3. Melody items: Wind Melody, Lola's Melody, and Memory Melody share FluteMusicActorController for music playback. Requires Will (form 0). Each melody handler verifies the target scene, spawns the music actor with a melody index ($20 = 0/1/2), and the controller manages the full SPC upload → playback → poll → effect → restore cycle.

4. Dialogue option items: Herb (yes/no heal), Journal (3 topics), Hieroglyph Plates (6-slot puzzle with swap logic).

=== BUTTON AND DISPLAY CONVENTIONS ===
The use-item button is logical bit $0008 (db-us/transforms.json rewrites the vanilla $4000 constants of this block to $0008, and the vanilla $CFF0 joypadMaskStd constants to $CFFC). TSB joypadHeld consumes a button (joypadCurrent stops reporting it); TSB joypadMaskStd with $CFFC hides everything except Start/Select and bits 0-1 from joypadCurrent, D-pad included. Neither concerns the Start button.

=== SHARED HELPERS ===

FluteMusicActorController: Multi-phase actor orchestrating melody playback — enters display-filter mode, hides the buttons, spawns SPC transfer actors, overrides the player to a static pose, polls for music completion, dispatches to the melody-specific *_Effect handler via SwitchCase, then restores background music and leaves display-filter mode.

=== SPECIAL MECHANICS ===

Red Jewel: BCD arithmetic (SED/CLD) for decimal jewel counter. Spawns an orbit visual effect that expands from diameter 1 to 255 via ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef.

Hieroglyph Plates: Items $1E–$23 share one handler. Plate ID = item − $1E. Six slots stored at $0B28 (word each, $FFFF = empty). Placing a plate in an occupied slot swaps the old plate back to inventory via GiveItemToPlayer.

Aura: Shadow-only (form 2), requires stationary player with no active dialogue/cutscene flags. Triggers transformation via player actor function pointer override to PlayerAuraTransformEntry.

Gorgon Flower: Three independent petal flags ($BF/$C0/$C1). Item is only removed when all three are set — partial placement persists across visits.

Inca Statues A/B: two mantels in scene $1E, statue A at tiles ($37-$38, $12-$13) and statue B at ($26-$27, $15-$16); standing on the other statue's mantel prints the shape-mismatch message. db-us/transforms.json (block item_use_system) repairs four vanilla branch quirks: (1) the four branches in the primary tile checks (two to loc_0386EA in A, two to loc_038800 in B) jumped into the middle of the CheckAlt routine, past its Y test, and now target the start of UseItem_IncaStatueA_CheckAlt / UseItem_IncaStatueB_CheckAlt; (2) the last X test of each CheckAlt routine (CMP #$27 in A, CMP #$38 in B) used a BNE whose target was the very next instruction, so the second tile of the mantel never reported a mismatch; it becomes BEQ to the mismatch message (UseItem_IncaStatueA_Mismatch / UseItem_IncaStatueB_Mismatch). The two rewrites in (2) span a line break, so extract:lt text (address tags between the lines) still shows the vanilla BNE, and a rebuild from extract:lt output lacks them (OQ-I026-1).

=== WRAM VARIABLES ===

$0AA6: Current hieroglyph plate ID (item index − $1E)
$0AAC: Hieroglyph slot selection (0–5)
$0B28: Hieroglyph slot table (6 words; $FFFF = empty, else plate ID)

mode7_perspective:
Mode 7 perspective thinker (Bank 03, 239936-240520). Every frame it rebuilds three 224-line HDMA tables that drive the Mode 7 matrix registers M7A-M7D, so the flat Mode 7 plane is rotated by an angle index and gets a perspective gradient (the zoom grows from the top scanline to the bottom one).

=== ENTRY POINTS ===

- Mode7PerspectiveInit is a thinker-def <#04,#08>: the two header bytes are the word $0804 that goes into animScratch2. Bit 2 puts the thinker into RunThinkers_Hdma, which runs after ResetHdmaState every frame; the four HDMA channels queued below are therefore re-armed each frame. Bit 11 is the lighter-frame flag. Only the scene thinker list of scene $FE (the world map, thinker_spawn_0CEB3D = Init + IrisCircleEffect) spawns it through the list.
- Init has no RTL: it falls straight into Mode7PerspectiveUpdate (the Update block starts at the byte after Init's last STA).
- Four actor scripts spawn Mode7PerspectiveUpdate directly with COP SpawnThinker and skip Init: pr8C_prologue1 and pr8C_prologue5 (prologue prophecy), garden_crash_cutscene (Sky Garden crash) and future_vision_cutscene (Angkor Wat). SpawnThinker does not read the thinker-def header, so each of them stores $0804 into the new thinker's animScratch2 itself, writes M7SEL = 0 (map repeats) and drives the three parameters below from a companion script.

=== PARAMETERS (global low-RAM words, not actor fields) ===

The thinker reads absolute low-RAM words (D is forced to 0), so every script writes them with STA $00B8 style absolute stores. They are not per-thinker fields.

| Word | Role here | Written by |
|------|-----------|------------|
| $00B8 | Starting divisor ('scale'). The quotient is abs(cos) / divisor in 8.8 fixed point, so $80 is about 1:1 ($7FFF / $80 = $FF), a smaller divisor zooms out and a larger one zooms in. Init sets $0400 | Cutscene controllers (future vision $001C up to $0080, prologue $0020), WorldMapController (adds gravity deltas) |
| $00B6 | Divisor increment per scanline, 8.8 fixed point. 0 gives a flat plane without perspective. Init sets 0 | Prologue controllers ($0280 / $0200 counted down towards 0), future vision (INC), WorldMapController (descent loop subtracts $10 per frame) |
| $00BC | Rotation index. ($BC AND $01FF) x 2 indexes the 512-step sine and cosine tables (0.703 degrees per step). Init sets 0 | Cutscenes INC it; WorldMapController route steps add their third delta axis to it (its own comments call that axis elevation) |
| $00CA / $00CC | Mode 7 centre X / Y (copied to M7X / M7Y by the NMI). Init takes them from worldMapPlayerX / Y ($0D54 / $0D56) | Init, the cutscene controllers, WorldMapController |

=== ONE-TIME TABLE FILL ===

The first tick writes 224 entries of {count 1, data word 0} plus a $00 terminator into $7E7000 (M7A), $7E7800 (M7B) and $7E8000 (M7C): 673 bytes each. A count of 1 with bit 7 clear is a one-scanline, non-repeat entry. COP SetEntryHere follows, so only the data words are rewritten on later frames.

=== PER-FRAME COMPUTATION ===

1. D := 0. Scratch is absolute $00-$04, $0E, $18 and $1C. $00/$01 := 0 (this clears the fraction byte $01), $02 := $B8 (the divisor word $02/$03), $04 := $B6, $0E := 224.
2. Y = ($BC AND $1FF) x 2. cos is read from cosine_table_16bit[Y] and sin from sine_table_16bit[Y] ($7FFF = 1.0). Both tables are read past their nominal length on purpose (math_lookup_tables adjacency contract). The absolute values go to $18 (|cos|) and $1C (|sin|); the two signs choose one of four routines.
3. PEA QueueMode7HdmaTables-1 makes the routine's final RTS continue in the queue code (return-address trick).
4. NormalizeDivisor shifts $02, $18, $1C and $04 right together until the divisor word has no high byte. The quotients do not change; the 8-bit WRDIVB divisor input is satisfied.
5. For each of the 224 scanlines: divide |cos| by the divisor with the hardware 16/8 divider, divide |sin|, store the signed results into the three tables, then add $04 to the 16-bit word at $01/$02. $01 is the fraction byte and $02 the low byte of the divisor word, so this adds $B6 / 256 to the divisor: the divisor, and with it the zoom, grows down the screen.
6. If that add carries out of $02, the carry is added to $03 and |cos|, |sin|, the divisor word and $04 are all halved. Their ratios are kept and the divisor returns to 8 bits. The fraction byte $01 is not halved.

| Case | M7A (table $7E7000) | M7B ($7E7800) | M7C ($7E8000) |
|------|---------------------|---------------|---------------|
| +cos, +sin | +cos/div | +sin/div | -sin/div |
| +cos, -sin | +cos/div | -abs(sin)/div | +abs(sin)/div |
| -cos, +sin | -abs(cos)/div | +sin/div | -sin/div |
| -cos, -sin | -abs(cos)/div | -abs(sin)/div | +abs(sin)/div |

In every case A = D = cos/div, B = sin/div and C = -sin/div: the rotation matrix divided by the per-scanline divisor.

=== HDMA QUEUE ===

QueueMode7HdmaTables issues four COP QueueHdmaDirect. The second operand is a B-bus register index (#1B..#1E = $211B..$211E), not a channel number. QueueHdmaDirect sets up a DIRECT-table HDMA channel on the next free channel (cop_handlers_hdma_dma), so four channels are used per frame and released again by the next ResetHdmaState. Table A is queued twice, for M7A and for M7D.

=== QUIRKS ===

- M7SEL = $80 written by Init means: tilemap repeat off and non-tilemap fill = 0, i.e. the area outside the 1024x1024 map is transparent (nesdev PPU registers). The cutscene spawners write M7SEL = 0 instead, which repeats the map.
- $B6 is the per-scanline divisor increment, not a rotation angle; the rotation is $BC.
- STY $WRDIVB with 16-bit Y also writes $4207 (HTIMEL) with the divisor high byte, which is 0 here. No H-IRQ use was checked.
- Quadrants 3 and 4 use 4 NOPs where 1 and 2 use 6: the extra LDA #0 / SEC before the SBC fill the divider's 16-cycle delay (derived from cycle counts, not run).
- The three tables live at $7E7000, $7E7800 and $7E8000, the same addresses as tileStagingBuffer and as buffers of scanline_band_hdma_thinker (its buffers are $7000, $7400, $7800, $7C00, $8000 and $8400). Not traced: whether any scene runs both.
- Init writes $FFFF to the words $7F0B22 and $7F0B24. No reader was found in extracted/.
mode7_perspective_unused:
Unused Mode 7 perspective variant — alternate HDMA table generation with indirect headers (240520–241015, Bank 03).

An earlier or alternate implementation of the Mode 7 perspective rotation system (compare mode7_perspective at 239936). Never referenced by any scene actor, thinker spawn, or COP handler in the shipped ROM. Uses the same sine/cosine tables and 4-quadrant hardware divide approach but differs in several significant ways.

=== DIFFERENCES FROM ACTIVE VERSION (mode7_perspective) ===

1. HDMA table format: Uses 3-entry indirect HDMA headers. Each table gets three $F0 (240) scanline-count entries at offset 0/3/6, with WRAM data addresses ($7100/$71E0 for M7A, $7900/$79E0 for M7B, $8100/$81E0 for M7C) written as 16-bit words. Matrix data fills the data regions ($7E7100, $7E7900, $7E8100) separately.

2. Fill direction: X starts at $01C0 and decrements (DEX×2), filling data regions from high offset to low. The active version fills from X=$0000 upward.

3. Perspective direction: Subtracts rotation increment (SEC/SBC $04) instead of adding (CLC/ADC). This inverts the foreshortening — near scanlines would be scaled more than distant ones.

4. No NormalizeDivisor: Does not pre-normalize the divisor to fit 8 bits. If scale ($B8) exceeds 255, the hardware divide would receive a truncated divisor, producing incorrect results. The active version right-shifts all operands until the divisor fits.

5. Underflow handling: Uses BCC/DEC $03 (borrow detection) instead of BCS/INC $03 (carry detection), matching the subtraction-based accumulation.

6. DMA command: Uses COP QueueHdma instead of COP QueueHdmaDirect.

7. NOP count: Quadrants 3/4 use only 4 NOPs (vs 6 in Q1/Q2) — fewer hardware divide delay cycles, potentially reading results too early on some hardware revisions.

Likely superseded by mode7_perspective during development due to the missing divisor normalization and simpler per-scanline table format.
oam_digit_compose:
OAM digit sprite composition (244449–244613, Bank 03).

Converts a packed BCD number into individual digit sprites in the OAM compose buffer ($7F3100). Callers: SpawnDamageNumberEffect (floating damage numbers, via ComposeDigitSprites), the three-two-one countdown digits in ec11_countdown, mu67_bomb and it1B_trial (ComposeDigitSprites), the diary counter (ComposeDigitSprites_AtCursor) and the unused AttackTrailShort.

=== PACKED BCD FORMAT ===

Input at DP $0000 is a 16-bit packed value (FormatDamageDigits produces it; the countdown scripts store 1, 2 or 3 directly):
- Byte $0001 (high byte), low nibble = hundreds digit (0–9)
- Byte $0000 (low byte), bits 7–4 = tens digit (0–9)
- Byte $0000 (low byte), bits 3–0 = ones digit (0–9)

Digits are rendered left-to-right: hundreds → tens → ones. Leading zeros are skipped (no sprite) but still advance the cursor by 4px; the ones digit is always drawn. Drawn digits advance the cursor by 8px.

=== OAM BUFFER ENTRY FORMAT ===

Each digit produces a 6-byte entry in the compose buffer at $7F3100 (world coordinates; RenderComposeBuffer subtracts the scroll):
- Bytes 0–1: X position (16-bit)
- Bytes 2–3: Y position (16-bit)
- Bytes 4–5: tile word = ($70 + digit) | the attribute word in DP $0002 (callers use $3200 or $2200: priority and palette bits)

The buffer write cursor at $00D8 advances by 6 per entry. No end marker is written here; the main loop in system_core writes the $FF terminator at the cursor after all actors have run.

=== ENTRY CONDITIONS (ComposeDigitSprites) ===

- DP $0000: packed BCD value
- DP $0014: actor X position (first digit X = actorX − 12)
- DP $0016: Y position of the digits (used unchanged)
- DP $000E: tile attribute word (copied to DP $0002)
- $00D8: OAM compose buffer write cursor

Scratch used: DP $0002 (attribute), $0018 (digit X cursor), $001C (digit Y). ComposeDigitSprites_AtCursor instead expects the caller to have set $0018, $001C and $0002 itself.
radar_map_screen:
Radar map screen overlay — the Start-button map of the current area (229567–230416, Bank 03).

Draws a 17×17-cell view centered on the player. One cell = 4×4 map tiles (64×64 px) = one BG3 tilemap word. Contents: an icon for every unopened treasure chest, a dot for every actor flagged extendedFlags bit 8 (the stat-bearing enemies counted in enemiesRemainingBcd), a second dot type for actors flagged bit 9 (only dark_space.asm sets that bit, so these are probably Dark Space entrances: OQ-63), and a legend with the unopened-chest count and the remaining-enemy count. When the scene still offers an unclaimed clear reward (enemy_clear_reward_table, flag $0300 + scene), a framed 2×2 reward icon and a BG3 label are added. GlobalInputHandler calls RadarScreenSetup once when Start opens the map and RadarBorderAnimate every frame of its display loop.

=== RENDERING PIPELINE (RadarScreenSetup) ===

1. Wait until no adhoc VRAM DMA is pending, then queue 512 bytes of radar icon graphics (radar_icons_001C00) for VRAM $7700 and wait for that transfer to finish.
2. Clear the BG3 staging buffer and block-copy the radar layout (radar_layout_001E00, $0580 bytes) to $7F0380.
3. Compute the 68×68-tile viewport (player tile aligned down to a multiple of 4, minus 32 on each axis). Left/right/top/bottom are kept in WRAM scratch $0018/$001A/$001C/$001E.
4. RadarPlotSceneMarkers draws the unopened chests inside the viewport and returns the count of all unopened chests of the scene (BCD, in scratch $0002); the count is shown as digits at $7F07CC/$7F07CE next to the chest icon $2EE6.
5. The viewport bounds are converted from tiles to pixels (×16) and RadarPlotActors plots the dots.
6. The remaining-enemy count (enemiesRemainingBcd, BCD) is shown as digits at $7F060C/$7F060E next to the dot icon $2AE7.
7. If flag $0300 + sceneCurrent is clear and enemy_clear_reward_table[scene] is non-zero, the reward frame is drawn and the BG3 script system_strings.consolestring_01EAD1 runs for the text.
8. Sets displayModeFlags bit 0, which requests a full BG3 staging upload.

=== RADAR RESOLUTION ===

Map tiles are 16 px, so a 4-tile cell is 64 px. Chest records hold tile coordinates: cell column byte offset = ((tileX − left) >> 1) AND $FE, row = (((tileY − top) >> 1) AND $FE) << 5 (64 bytes per tilemap row). Actors hold pixel coordinates: column = ((x − left) >> 5) AND $FFFE, row = (y − top) AND $FFC0. Both give the same cell grid; $0216 is added as the byte offset of the radar interior inside the $7F0200 buffer.

=== BORDER ANIMATION ===

RadarBorderAnimate runs on odd frames only. It steps an index (kept in a word on the caller's stack, $03,S) through the 29-entry RadarBorderColorTable and writes the entry to $7F0A24, which is cgramPalette color 18. The table values are BGR555 colors (a blue → yellow → blue cycle), so the border shimmers by palette cycling, not by changing tiles.
save_system:
SRAM save/load system — game-state persistence with dual-checksum validation (252182–252392, Bank 03).

Provides the save slot infrastructure. Four save slots are supported, each occupying 512 bytes of SRAM at $306200 + (slot × 512): 508 bytes of data followed by two checksum words at +$1FC and +$1FE.

=== SAVE/LOAD ===

SaveGameState_Scene copies 508 bytes of WRAM ($0A00–$0BFB) to SRAM after storing the current scene ID at $0B06. LoadGameState_Scene reverses the process after verifying integrity. Both routines mask the slot number to 0–3 and compute the SRAM offset via XBA + ASL (slot × 256 × 2 = slot × 512).

The saved range is named eventFlags ($0A00) but holds more than event flags: it also contains the player stats and inventory state the engine keeps in that page (e.g. abilityBitmask $0AA2, playerMaxHp $0ACA, playerHp $0ACE, gemCount $0AD6) and the hieroglyph plate slots ($0B28–$0B32).

=== INTEGRITY VERIFICATION ===

ComputeSaveChecksum generates two checksums over each slot's 508 bytes (254 words):
- Additive checksum ($0018): running sum of all data words
- XOR checksum ($001C): running XOR of all data words

Both are seeded with the constant $3652, so a zeroed slot computes $3652/$3652 and never matches the stored zeros. Both are order-independent, so swapped words go undetected; the pair mainly guards against corrupted or missing data.

=== SLOT MANAGEMENT ===

ClearSaveSlot fills an entire 512-byte slot with zeros, erasing both the data and the stored checksums, so LoadGameState_Scene fails the checksum compare (carry set).

Load returns carry CLEAR on success, carry SET on failure (corrupt or empty). ClearSaveSlot returns carry SET to match the empty-slot convention.
scene_lifecycle:
Scene lifecycle management — transitions, state initialization, and resource loading (252392–254128, Bank 03).

Contains the complete scene transition pipeline: detecting pending transitions, executing visual exit/enter effects, clearing state, loading scene resources (HUD, palettes, player graphics, camera bounds), and spawning actors.

=== TRANSITION PIPELINE ===

CheckSceneTransition → ExecuteSceneTransition orchestrates the full scene change:
1. Run ScreenExitTransition (if world is active)
2. Clear the world-ready flag, clear the HDMA enable mask, disable NMI (DisableNmiKeepJoypad leaves only joypad auto-read on) and enter forced blank
3. Resolve target scene: a staged world-map entry ($0D52/$0D53 nonzero → scene $FE) or sceneNext (normal)
4. ClearSceneState: comprehensive reset of all game variables, followed by scene script execution, camera init, event blocks, actor spawning, collision setup, palette/graphics loading, and initial tilemap rendering
5. Run ScreenEnterTransition
6. Optional: wait for a button press while the scene-title box is shown ($00B4 set by DisplaySceneTitle)

=== VISUAL TRANSITIONS ===

ScreenExitTransition and ScreenEnterTransition each support 4–5 transition effect types. The exit type is the low byte of gfxCacheIdxA ($0648) and the enter type is its high byte ($0649); the speed (frame delay) is likewise the low byte of gfxCacheIdxB ($064A) for exit and its high byte ($064B) for enter. Cutscene scripts write these words before COP QueueMapChange and ExecuteSceneTransition clears them afterwards, so despite the names they are transition parameters, not graphics-cache indices:
- Type 0: Graduated brightness fade (frame delay per brightness step = speed byte)
- Type 1: Instant blank/display
- Type 2: Mosaic dissolve with brightness fade
- Type 3: Sine-wave HDMA scroll distortion with brightness fade
- Type 4 (exit only): Alternative wave pattern (ScreenExitTransition_WaveAlt)

Wave transitions use ApplyScrollWaveEffect and ComputeSineScrollTable to build per-scanline horizontal scroll offsets via hardware multiply, driving HDMA channels 6 and 7. DP $006E is the wave amplitude (grows during exit, shrinks during enter) and $0070 the spatial frequency (6); the wave's motion over time comes from the NMI frame counter $36.

=== SCENE RESOURCE LOADING (ClearSceneState) ===

ClearSceneState is the ‘big setup’ function that calls into multiple engine subsystems to prepare a new scene:
- SceneScriptMain: parse scene definition (tileset, tilemap, music, display config)
- InitCameraBounds: set camera limits from map geometry or custom packed bounds
- ApplyAllEventBlocks: apply persistent tile modifications from event flags
- PlaceOpenedChestTiles: redraw the chests of scene_chest_table whose event flag is set as open chests in the map
- Actor/thinker spawning and initialization via actor_execution
- LoadScenePalettes / LoadPlayerGraphics: character/form-dependent resource loading
- CameraFullRefresh or RenderPaletteTiles: initial tilemap rendering depending on scroll mode
sprite_composition:
Sprite composition, depth sorting, OAM table construction, and render list management (247295–248565 + 252010–252033, Bank 03).

Implements the complete pipeline for converting actor metasprite definitions into the hardware OAM table each frame. The system processes the actor linked list in four stages: render list clearing, depth sorting, metasprite decomposition, and OAM table packing.

=== RENDER LIST CLEARING (ClearActorRenderList, 252010) ===

ClearActorRenderList zeroes the 512-byte depth-sort bucket array at $0200–$03FE and writes a $FFFF end sentinel at $0400, preparing it for SortActorsByDepth. It is called at scene setup (scene_lifecycle, inventory_overlay), not every frame: SortActors_BuildFinalList re-zeroes each bucket it consumes (a PHA written over the popped bucket word), so the array is already clean at the start of the next frame's sort.

=== DEPTH SORTING (SortActorsByDepth) ===

Uses a bucket sort algorithm with the $0200–$03FE WRAM region as a bucket array indexed by sort key. Each actor's screen-space Y position is converted to an inverted sort key (lower on screen = lower key = emitted first = lowest OAM index, which the PPU draws in front of higher indexes). The stack pointer is repurposed to iterate the sort buffer efficiently via PLX/PLA.

Sort key assignment based on actor flags ($10):
- Bit 13 ($2000): Actor hidden — skipped entirely
- Bits 0+1 ($0003) both clear: Y-based depth key (screen Y inverted via EOR, doubled via ASL)
- Bit 0 only ($0001): Fixed key $01FE — emitted last = highest OAM index = always behind (COP SetPriorityMin sets this bit)
- Bit 1 ($0002): Fixed key $0000 — emitted first = OAM index 0 = always in front (COP SetPriorityMax); wins when both bits are set

BuildFinalList reads the bucket array front-to-back via PLY (SP set to $01FF), producing the final depth-sorted actor list at $0C00.

=== SPRITE COMPOSITION (ComposeAllSprites) ===

Entry point called from the main game loop after actor execution. Pre-fills the entire 128-entry OAM table with the hidden value $E080 (X byte $80, Y byte $E0 — Y $E0 is below the 224-line screen), then processes two sprite sources:
1. Compose buffer at $7F3100 (pre-composed sprites from damage digits, VFX)
2. Sorted actor list at $0C00 (metasprite decomposition per actor)

For each actor, dispatches to DecomposeActorMetasprites (generic) or DecomposePlayerSprites (player, identified by bit 15 of $10).

=== OAM TABLE LAYOUT ===

SNES OAM: 128 entries × 4 bytes at $0422–$0621, plus a 32-byte high table at $0622–$0641 (write pointer in $06). Each low-table entry: byte 0 = X[7:0], byte 1 = Y, bytes 2-3 = tile/attribute. The high table packs 2 bits per sprite (X bit 8, size flag) into groups of 4 via a rolling shift register ($00) with a 4-sprite counter ($0E).

=== METASPRITE FORMAT ===

7 bytes per sub-sprite in a metasprite definition:
- Byte 0: Size/priority flags (bit 0 → OAM hi-table size bit)
- Bytes 1-2: X offset pair (swapped via XBA when H-mirrored)
- Bytes 3-4: Y offset pair (swapped via XBA when V-mirrored)
- Bytes 5-6: Tile index + palette/priority attributes

Mirroring comes from the actor's OAM attribute word ($000E,X, copied to $04): bit 14 (H-flip) swaps the X offset pair and bit 15 (V-flip) swaps the Y offset pair, each tested via the carry from ASL. The whole word is also EOR'd into every sub-sprite's tile/attribute word, so $0E acts as an XOR mask for flips, palette and priority (see cop_handlers_oam_attribs).

=== PLAYER SPRITE HANDLING ===

DecomposePlayerSprites adds character-form body table lookups (tile source address and bank), a per-sub-sprite list of tile source pointers at $06FF+ that DmaPlayerTilesToVram streams to VRAM, sequential OAM tile numbering, and sprite cache validation ($09CC/$09CE) to skip the re-upload when the metasprite pointer and bank haven't changed.

=== COMPOSE BUFFER ($7F3100) ===

Pre-composed sprite buffer for systems that generate sprites outside the metasprite pipeline (damage digits, visual effects). Each entry: X position (2B) + Y position (2B) + tile/attribute (2B), in world coordinates (RenderComposeBuffer subtracts the scroll). A word with bit 15 set ($FFFF, written by the main loop at oamWriteOffset) ends the buffer. RenderComposeBuffer runs before the actor metasprite loop, so these sprites take the lowest OAM indexes and draw in front of every actor.

=== ANIMATION (UpdateActorAnimation) ===

Indexes into the spriteset → animation → frame hierarchy to advance an actor's current animation. Returns carry set on sequence end (negative frame data), signaling the actor to loop or transition.
thinker_execution:
Thinker execution system — spawning, scheduling, and per-frame dispatch (250157–250357 + 251879–252010, Bank 03).

Manages the lifecycle and per-frame execution of scene thinkers — lightweight script actors that run alongside the main actor system. Thinkers handle ambient effects, palette cycling, background animations, cutscene overlays, and HDMA-driven visual effects.

=== THINKER DATA MODEL ===

Thinkers use a separate memory pool from actors (16 slots of $10 bytes at $0F00, allocated via ThinkerPoolAlloc in actor_execution). Each thinker slot contains:
- $0000,X: Code entry point (word)
- $0002,X: Bank byte
- $0004,X: Previous link pointer (doubly-linked list)
- $0006,X: Next link pointer
- $0008,X: Wait counter (same semantics as actor $08: a stored n makes the thinker skip n passes)
- animScratch ($7F0000,X): Thinker-specific scratch fields
- animScratch2 ($7F000E,X): Thinker filter flags (first word of the thinker's code, i.e. the first two operands of its thinker-def)

The thinker linked list is rooted at $005A (head) and $005C (tail).

=== SPAWNING (SpawnSceneThinkers, 251879) ===

SpawnSceneThinkers reads scene_thinkers[$0646] to find the current scene's thinker definition list. If the pointer is zero or bit 7 ($0080) is set in the first data byte, the scene has no active thinkers.

For each thinker record (terminated by $FF byte):
1. Allocates a slot via actor_execution.ThinkerPoolAlloc
2. Links into a doubly-linked list ($0004 = prev, $0006 = next)
3. Calls InitThinkerFromSceneData to parse the binary record

InitThinkerFromSceneData reads a variable-length record: type byte → animScratch+2 ($7F0002,X; the thinker's spawn parameter, e.g. a palette bundle ID), code pointer → $42, bank byte → $44. Dereferences the code pointer to read its first word as animScratch2 (thinker filter flags), then stores entry point (code + 2) and bank to slot fields $0000/$0002.

=== EXECUTION TYPES (250157–250357) ===

Four runners filter the list on animScratch2 ($7F000E,X):

- RunThinkers_General: bit 2 ($0004) CLEAR. Called by MainLoop right after the VBlank sync and at scene start.
- RunThinkers_Hdma: bit 2 SET — the complement of RunThinkers_General. MainLoop and the scene-start sequence call it after ResetHdmaState, so the HDMA/window-DMA thinkers (the bit-2 ones: comet_lair_hdma_*, angel_tunnel_window_dma, ...) bind their channels after the per-frame reset.
- RunThinkers_General_Light: bit 11 ($0800) SET and bit 2 CLEAR. Called by the lighter frame routines of system_core (UpdateFrameDialogue, UpdateFrameRender, UpdateFrameFull) after their VBlank sync.
- RunThinkers_Hdma_Light: bits 11 AND 2 both SET. The same routines call it after ResetHdmaState, before the sync.

All 59 scene thinker-defs in extracted/ (32 with filter word $0804, 27 with $0800) have bit 11 set, so for scene thinkers RunThinkers_General_Light selects exactly the set of RunThinkers_General and RunThinkers_Hdma_Light exactly that of RunThinkers_Hdma. Runtime-spawned thinkers (SpawnThinker/SpawnThinkerParam, 77 sites) inherit the spawner's animScratch2 and some scripts store their own (future_vision_cutscene $0804, sE8_dark_gaia $0004, dc2F_adrift ORs in $0800), so there the bit does matter: a thinker without bit 11 runs only in the main loop (RunThinkers_General / RunThinkers_Hdma) and pauses while the lighter frame routines (dialogue, render, music upload) run. Bit 11 therefore reads as 'keep running in the lighter frame routines', not as a cutscene marker.

All four runners share one dispatch pattern: walk the list from $5A with D = X = slot, test the filter, then DEC $08 / BPL _Next (a wait counter of n skips n passes; the pass where it was 0 runs the script and STZ $08), push PHK + PEA _Next−1, the thinker's bank and entry − 1, and RTL into the script. The script runs like an actor script (COP ops, SetEntryHereAndYield, ends with RTL back to _Next). _Next follows the $06 link or exits when the list is exhausted.
tile_collision_physics:
Tile collision physics and axis-separated movement (250357–251879, Bank 03).

Implements actor movement with and without tile-based collision detection. The collision system uses axis-separated processing: X axis is resolved first (MoveLeft/MoveRight), then Y axis (MoveUp/MoveDown), each returning carry set on block or carry clear on pass.

=== MOVEMENT SYSTEM ===

Two movement entry points called from the actor execution post-tick:
- ApplyMovement: direct delta application with no collision — used when bit 3 ($0008) of $10 is clear, and always by RunActors_OverlayOnly
- ApplyMovementWithCollision: full tile collision pipeline, used when bit 3 ($0008) of $10 is set

Both read movement from either an override chain pointer ($2C/$2E → linked movement sources) or per-actor scratch fields (moveScratch1/moveScratch2 at $7F002C/$7F002E). Direction word $12 controls negation: bit 14 ($4000) flips X, bit 13 ($2000) flips Y.

=== COLLISION PIPELINE ===

For each axis, the pipeline:
1. Read delta from override or scratch
2. Negate per direction flags
3. PEA a post-collision handler as return address
4. JMP to MoveLeft/Right or MoveUp/Down based on delta sign
5. MoveXxx checks tiles along the leading edge of the hitbox
6. Returns carry set (blocked → position snapped to tile boundary) or carry clear (passed)
7. Post-collision handler applies residual movement and clears scratch

CollisionY_Setup includes a bounce mechanism: if both solid-contact ($10 bit 2) and bounce flag (extendedFlags bit 6 = $0040) are set, direction bits are reversed via EOR $6000 on $12.

=== TILE MAP FORMAT ===

The collision tile map is accessed via long pointer [$80] with offsets computed by CalcTileMapOffset. Each byte encodes two collision nibbles:
- High nibble ($F0): nonzero = immediately solid (wall)
- Low nibble ($0F): tile type for dispatch table (0 = passable/check-adjacent, 1–F = solid)

The map is stored as 256-byte pages of 16×16 tiles (a tile is 16×16 pixels). CalcTileMapOffset builds the offset as: high byte = page = (tileY >> 4) × mapRowStrideL0 ($0693) + (tileX >> 4); low byte = (tileY & $F) << 4 | (tileX & $F). So +$10 in the low byte steps one tile DOWN (+Y) and +1 steps one tile RIGHT (+X).

=== HITBOX DATA ===

Hitbox dimensions come from the metasprite header at [metaspritePtr]:
- $0000: X left offset (ORA #$FF00 forces the high byte, so it is always treated as negative: the byte must be ≥ $80)
- $0001: Y top offset (same treatment)
- $0002: X width in tiles (horizontal scan count for vertical edges)
- $0003: Y height in tiles (vertical scan count for horizontal edges)

For horizontal movement, the leading edge X is computed and tiles are scanned vertically across $0003 rows. For vertical movement, the leading edge Y is computed and tiles are scanned horizontally across $0002 columns.

=== POSITION SNAPPING ===

When collision occurs, BlockH/BlockV snap the actor position to the nearest tile boundary:
- Positive delta (moving right/down): AND $FFF0 (snap to left/top edge of blocking tile)
- Negative delta (moving left/up): AND $FFF0 + $0010 if sub-tile aligned (snap to right/bottom edge)

The hitbox offset is then subtracted to compute the final actor position. The snap uses only the left/top offset, so it leaves the hitbox flush against the blocking tile only for hitboxes one tile wide/tall.

=== SPECIAL TILES ===

CheckActorOnSpecialTile probes (actorX − 8, actorY − 16) for two tile patterns:
- Type $06 at the probe tile and at the diagonal (+X,+Y) neighbor
- Type $00 at the probe tile with type $09 at both the right (+X) and the below (+Y) neighbor (L-pattern)
When a pattern matches, the axis routine returns carry set immediately — the axis movement is dropped without snapping and without setting the solid-contact flag ($10 bit 2). Collision types $06 and $09 are not traced to a purpose.

world_map_route_table:
World map travel routes — movement step sequences for the trips of WorldMapController (241015–242132, Bank 03).

Pure data block: a pointer table of 38 entries ($00–$25; $00 aliases $01) to 37 route arrays. The arrays are named route_<id>_<origin>_to_<destination> (route_unused_<id> for $0E, $0F, $10, $23, $24 and $25, which nothing stages). The full trip list and the menu that stages each route are in the world_map_options block note.

=== DATA FORMAT ===

A step is four bytes, shown by the extraction as `route-step < xDeltaIndex, yDeltaIndex, rotationDeltaIndex, ticks >`:
  - Byte 0: index into move_chain_table for the X velocity chain ($00CA); 0 = still
  - Byte 1: index for the Y chain ($00CC); 0 = still
  - Byte 2: index for the rotation chain ($00BC); 0 = still
  - Byte 3: tick count n; the step runs n + 1 ticks
Every array is 4n + 1 bytes: a hidden $FF ends it ($FE, subroutine, is never used). The indices used are 1 (+1 per tick), 2 (-1), $11 (alternating +1, 0) and $12 (alternating -1, 0) for X and Y, and 1 (+1) or 2 (-1) for rotation; a step never mixes rotation with movement, so a route turns the map and runs straight in one of eight directions.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

The old header read the four bytes as flags (animation / speed nibbles), direction (turn left / right), a spare byte and a pixel distance; that reading is wrong, there are no turn codes and byte 3 is a tick count, not a distance.

There is no terminator entry: the strings follow the table directly, so an id that is not listed would run on into string bytes (no listed or staged scene does; OQ-I059-7).

- every overworld_exit scene: $01 $0A $15 $1C $32 $3E $69 $78 $82 $91 $A0 $AC $B0 $C3 $CC;
- every scene that starts a scripted trip: $06 $17 $1A $30 $39 $49 $6A $78 $79 $96 $AE $C8, and every scripted destination: $01 $15 $1A $1C $32 $49 $4B $78 $91 $AC $C4 $DC;
